decisions.reason: The Definition uses R without binding it, so interiority is not a predicate of the supplied data. Bound R>0 and epsilon>0 explicitly, retaining B(x,R epsilon+2h) subset Omega and specifying the chosen unscaled-kernel support bound. The finite integration-compatible partition, positive h and volumes, local volume bound and choice-free quadrature data are unchanged.

F2 omitted openness of U and support containment in T(U). For T:(0,1) into R the inclusion and a continuous nonzero bump supported near 2 give a positive full-space integral but zero transformed integral. This overstatement is nonfatal to the actual proof: reflection and positive scaling are global diffeomorphisms of R^d, all coordinate integrands are continuous and compactly supported, and oddness gives I=-I. Restated the exact supplier with zero extension; both moment conclusions are unchanged.

F3 overstates the supplier by replacing supp(f) subset T(U) with containment in an arbitrary codomain V and omitting open U. The inclusion (0,1) into R with a nonzero bump near 2 disproves that version. The actual map u to epsilon u is globally onto with determinant epsilon^d, so its moment substitutions are valid; chain rule gives the derivative powers and onto scaling gives equality of suprema. Repaired F3 only, leaving the Statement and proof intact; the support assertion includes closure because the scaled closed ball contains every nonzero point.

F4 falsely permits support merely in an arbitrary codomain: inclusion (0,1) into R and a nonzero continuous bump near 2 violate its formula. This is nonfatal to the theorem because y=x-epsilon u is globally onto with absolute determinant epsilon^d. Restored the exact open-domain/image-support/zero-extension conditions and made that single affine substitution explicit. Taylor on R^d gives |R| <= epsilon^3 ||D^3 f|| |u|^3/6; derivative moments annihilate the constant/quadratic terms and give +gradient f. Wrote the linear contraction with partial_j inside the sum, and retained the componentwise dual-unit-vector norm bound, including v=0, to obtain epsilon^2 m3/6. The Statement is unchanged.
